business_scope.primary_industry_name: Tier-3/4 Server Rack Space Leasing and Bare-Metal Server Hosting

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid: Quebec private law is civil law under the Civil Code of Quebec (CCQ), articles 2236-2252 governing sociétés en commandite (limited partnerships), overlaid by federal common-law statutes in criminal, taxation and AML/CFT matters; Quebec's enterprise registry regime is a statutory civil-law publicity system administered by the Registraire des entreprises du Québec.
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Canada-China Foreign Investment Promotion and Protection Agreement (FIPA, in force since December 1, 2014)
Canada-European Union Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA)
Canada-United Kingdom Free Trade Agreement (transitional continuation of CETA for UK)
Canada-China Double Taxation Agreement (1986, as amended by subsequent protocols)
Canada-United States Tax Convention (1980, as amended) and over 90 other active Canadian income tax treaties

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA), SC 2000, c. 17 and PCMLTF Regulations, SOR/2002-184; Criminal Code of Canada, RSC 1985, c. C-46 (money laundering and illicit financing offences); Quebec - Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c. P-44.1 (particularly sections 16.1-16.8 establishing the registre des particuliers/beneficial ownership registry and the obligation to identify ultimate beneficiaries); Regulation respecting the legal publicity of enterprises and the register of individuals, CQLR c. P-44.1, r. 3.2; Charter of the French Language, CQLR c. C-11.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Certificate of Status) of each corporate general partner and any corporate limited partner formed outside Canada
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent companies registry of the country of origin (e.g., State Administration for Market Regulation in China)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille pursuant to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention (in force for Canada since January 11, 2024; in force for China since November 7, 2023); for non-Convention jurisdictions, Canadian consular legalization through the competent Canadian diplomatic mission

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized certified copy of the corporate charter, articles of incorporation and recent registry extract of each foreign corporate partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or officially authorized authority in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Canadian consular legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copies of passports or national identity documents of all Ultimate Beneficial Owners (natural persons) holding 25% or more of the partnership
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or competent translator in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarial certificate followed by Hague Apostille or Canadian consular legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Corporate resolutions of each foreign corporate partner authorizing the formation of the Quebec LP, the capital commitment, and the appointment of the general partner and Quebec attorney-in-fact
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors of the foreign corporate partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Canadian consular legalization in the jurisdiction of incorporation

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against the United Nations Security Council Consolidated Lists, all Canadian sanctions lists under the Special Economic Measures Act (SEMA), the United Nations Act, the Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act (Magnitsky Act), and the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act, section 35; supplementary OFAC SDN screening is mandatory because the target payment rails include USD SWIFT wires and ACH; FINTRAC Politically Exposed Persons (PEP) due diligence guidance applies to foreign domestic PEPs and heads of international organizations, and extended due diligence (EDD) is required for high-risk jurisdictions; screening must be performed at admission of each partner, at each capital event, and annually thereafter, with all results logged in the compliance file.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (Quebec Business Registry) - www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca, online module 'Renez' (name reservation service)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Charter of the French Language, CQLR c. C-11, and the Regulation respecting the language of commerce and business, CQLR c. C-11, r. 9, the partnership's name must have a French version and be in French in all legal acts and commercial documents within Quebec; transliterations must be exact; Latin-script characters are required; an English or other-language version may be registered only where the French version already exists, and the French name prevails for legal publicity purposes.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank / Banque (requires OSFI or related regulatory approval)
Lawyer / Avocat (requires Barreau du Québec consent)
Engineer / Ingénieur (requires Ordre des ingénieurs consent)
Doctor / Médecin (requires Collège des médecins consent)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Extensions: before expiry of the 90-day reservation, the applicant may file a request for renewal via the REQ online portal; the registrar has discretion to grant one additional period upon payment of the applicable fee; if extension is denied or expires, a new name reservation application must be filed de novo. Rejection appeal: within 30 days of the refusal notice, the applicant must file a written application for administrative review with the Registraire's review department, including legal and linguistic arguments establishing distinctiveness, non-misleading character, and compliance with the French-language rules; if the registrar confirms the refusal, an appeal may be brought before the Tribunal administratif du Québec (TAQ) within the statutory deadline (generally 30 days), naming the Registraire as respondent.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Limited permissibility: the declared registered office must be a real physical address in Quebec at which legal service of process can be made and partnership records are available for inspection; a serviced office or business-centre address in Quebec may be accepted at initial registration, but a pure virtual mailbox without a physical operational presence is not commercially or tax-substance compliant for a data-center colocation lessor, and banks, insurers and anchor tenants will require a genuine Quebec establishment.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-moderate for a standard non-licensed information-technology activity: estimated 10%-15% annual risk of an unannounced inspection by the Registraire, Revenu Québec or the Canada Revenue Agency; probability rises to approximately 25%-40% if the registered office is a virtual-only mailbox, if the UBO registry filings are inconsistent, or if inter-affiliate lease payments trigger tax-audit flags.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff under CQLR c. P-44.1, r. 1

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff under CQLR c. P-44.1, r. 1

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Filing of ultimate beneficial owner (registre des particuliers) declaration for partners holding 25% or more
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff under CQLR c. P-44.1, r. 3.2

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Drafting of the limited partnership agreement (contrat de société en commandite), corporate resolutions, Quebec minute book, and civil-law legal opinion for non-resident partners
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Private Quebec law firm (civil law counsel)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark (CAD 250-400 per hour; fixed-fee engagement)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization and certified true-copy authentication of the corporate due-diligence and UBO document bundle
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary public in Quebec and foreign notarial authorities
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for notarial tariffs

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Hague Apostille or Canadian consular legalization fees for foreign-origin documents (4-document bundle)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Foreign Ministry of Foreign Affairs or Canadian diplomatic/consular mission
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official government tariff of issuing state

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: PEP, OFAC, UN, and Canadian sanctions screening plus UBO verification through commercial compliance database
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark per screened entity

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office and service-of-process address in Quebec (first year, serviced office)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Registered-office service provider / commercial serviced office

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Civil Code of Québec (CCQ, CQLR c. CCQ-1996), arts. 2236-2248 (société en commandite); Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises (CQLR c. P-44.1), ss. 21-31; Règlement sur le registre des entreprises (CQLR c. P-44.1, r. 4)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (Québec Enterprise Registrar) — registre des entreprises sector, Gouvernement du Québec
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Déclaration d'immatriculation d'une société en commandite (Declaration of Registration of a Limited Partnership) filed under s. 21 of the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; capital is established by the partnership agreement and may be contributed in cash, property or services. For a non-financial data center colocation business, no escrow account is required; capital calls and contribution schedules are recorded in the partnership register.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST RESOLUTION OF THE GENERAL PARTNER OF THE LIMITED PARTNERSHIP: RESOLVED, that the capital subscriptions offered to the initial limited partners, as stated in the Limited Partnership Agreement, are hereby accepted and shall be recorded in the partnership register; RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Limited Partnership be established at [Address], Montréal, Québec, and that an address-change and initial registration declaration be filed with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec; and RESOLVED, that [Name] is appointed as General Partner and [Name] as Authorized Signatory, with authority to open bank accounts, sign leases, obtain municipal permits, and conduct all colocation business on ordinary terms.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec via the online portal registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation request (Demande de réservation de nom) through the Registraire's electronic platform, listing up to three proposed names. The chosen name must include the mandatory legal element 'S.E.C.' or the expression 'en commandite' and must not conflict with existing Quebec enterprise names or federally protected marks. Pay the reservation fee and cite the registration number in the subsequent declaration.
required_dossiers: Proposed name list (up to 3 choices)
Identification documents of the general partner
Mandate form if filing through a representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused for confusion or prohibited terms, the applicant may submit a new reservation request immediately; or file a written review application to the Registraire within 30 days. Adding distinctive geographic or descriptive elements usually cures the deficiency.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and Notarization of the Limited Partnership Agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notarial chamber of Quebec (optional for movable contributions) / private writing between the partners
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Contrat de société en commandite setting out the general partner's management rights, limited partner capital commitments, profit and loss allocations, transfer restrictions, and dissolution events. If any partner contributes real immovable property, the agreement must be executed before a Quebec notary and published in the Land Register to perfect ownership transfer. Otherwise, the agreement may be executed as a private instrument under the Civil Code of Québec.
required_dossiers: Identification of all general and limited partners
Schedule of initial contributions and capital accounts
Partnership register (register des sociétés en commandite)
Minute book and resolutions of the general partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Ambiguities are cured by a supplementary private amendment; if land rights are involved, the rectification must be re-notarized and published at the Land Registry office. Partner ratification instruments resolve signature defects.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Initial Registration with the Québec Enterprise Registrar
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec — electronic declaration service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete and file the Déclaration d'immatriculation d'une société en commandite (Form DE-2) online. Indicate the partnership name, the registered office address in Québec, the place of establishment, the general partner's identifiers, and any limited partners holding an interest exceeding 25% or otherwise requiring disclosure. Pay the CAD 120 registry fee. The Registraire then issues the Enterprise Number (NEQ) and the certificate of registration of the partnership.
required_dossiers: Name reservation certificate
Executed limited partnership agreement or notarial extract
Identification of the general partner and disclosable limited partners
Proof of registered office address (lease or municipal lease acknowledgement)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registraire issues a refusal or query under the legal publicity act, the filer may correct and resubmit the declaration through the online regularization module; a failure to regularize within 30 days can be administratively appealed before the Cour du Québec. Late-filing penalties are avoided by prompt correction.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Federal and Provincial Tax Registrations and Governance Formalities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) and Revenu Québec; financial institution for account opening
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply to the CRA Business Registry for a Business Number (BN) and register for GST/HST (Quebec uses GST at 5% plus QST at 9.975% collected through Revenu Québec). Register with Revenu Québec for QST, employer payroll source deductions, and the RL-1/RL-15 reporting accounts. Open a partnership bank account presenting the NEQ certificate, the partnership agreement, and the first resolution of the general partner. Maintain the partnership register and minute book at the registered office.
required_dossiers: NEQ certificate from the Registraire des entreprises
Limited partnership agreement and general partner resolution
RC1 Request for a Business Number form or online CRA intake
Revenu Québec registration for QST accounts
Bank account opening KYC/AML documentation (beneficial owners of general and limited partners)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA delays the BN issuance, the applicant may contact the CRA Business Window using the online case number. Revenu Québec errors are rectified via the 'Mon dossier' portal; disputes on concurrent GST/QST registrations are resolved by ensuring the BN entity and NEQ entity match before the first return filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Industrial and Physical Licensing Compliance for the Data Center
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ville de Montréal (borough permit counter and Service de sécurité incendie de Montréal, SIM); Régie du bâtiment du Québec (RBQ)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the data center's certificat d'occupation (occupancy certificate) at the borough permit office that has jurisdiction over the colocation site. Submit floor plans sealed by a professional engineer demonstrating structural capacity for raised floors, server racks, and battery rooms, and demonstrating compliance with the Québec Construction Code (Chapter 1, Building). Register the workplace with CNESST and obtain the prior fire safety inspection from SIM covering alarm systems, standby generators, and egress routes. If construction or major fit-out is involved, require the general contractor to hold a valid RBQ license.
required_dossiers: Occupancy certificate application with building plot plan
Structural and mechanical plans certified by an OIQ engineer
Fire safety plan and simulation documents for SIM inspection
RBQ contractor license attestation if fit-out construction exceeds exemption thresholds
CNESST workplace registration confirmation
CPR/ULC certificates for standby generators and electrical distribution
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipality refuses the occupancy certificate, the applicant may amend the plans and resubmit, or request a minor variance through the local zoning review committee. A dispute on fire code requirements is appealable to the municipal fire commissioner; unresolved RBQ technical objections may be referred to the tribunal administratif du logement for a conformity ruling.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Régie du bâtiment du Québec (RBQ) — Direction de l'application des règles techniques de construction; Ville de Montréal permit counters and Service de sécurité incendie de Montréal (SIM)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Certificat d'occupation (municipal occupancy certificate) coupled with RBQ conformity attestation for mechanical, electrical and fire safety installations of the colocation facility

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP) — Direction de l'évaluation environnementale
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category 2 (registration/declaration) under the Règlement sur l'encadrement d'activités en fonction de leur impact sur l'environnement (REAFIE) for diesel standby generators and air-conditioning systems. A full EIA (Category 1) is not required for standard colocation leasing unless the facility is located in a protected area or stores more than 3,000 litres of diesel fuel, in which case an attestation notice from MELCCFP is mandatory.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Cooling water discharges must meet the municipal sewer by-law parameters (pH 6.0-9.5, free chlorine less than 5 mg/L, temperature below 40°C). Standby generators must comply with the Quebec Clean Air Regulation (CQLR c. Q-2, r. 4.1) and the CCME Canadian ambient air quality standards for NOx and PM2.5. Spent UPS batteries, waste oil and coolants are managed under the Règlement sur les matières dangereuses (CQLR c. Q-2, r. 32) with manifests filed in the MELCCFP hazardous waste tracking system; battery waste is subject to the provincial recovery regulation for hazardous household materials.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification requires compliance with the Québec Construction Code (Chapitre I, Bâtiment) and the National Fire Protection Association codes applicable to data centers (NFPA 75 and NFPA 110 for emergency generators), including an SIM pre-operational inspection of alarm, standpipe/sprinkler, and generator systems. Structural load inspections must be sealed by a Quebec professional engineer for raised access floors (minimum 8 kPa), battery containment, and rack loading zones. Occupational clearance requires CNESST workplace registration and, where employees are present, an up-to-date prevention program for electrical safety and confined-space entry in cooling and power rooms.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) for federal GST/HST and income tax; Revenu Québec for Quebec QST and provincial income tax matters. Portals: CRA My Business Account (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/e-services/cra-login-services.html) and Revenu Québec CLIC (https://www.revenuquebec.ca/en/).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity not resident in Canada must first determine whether it carries on business in Canada. To obtain a GST/HST registration number, it must file Form RC1 (Request for GST/HST Registration), either through the CRA’s Business Registration Online portal or by written application, providing legal entity documentation, proof of foreign registration, and the intended Canadian permanent establishment details. For Quebec, the parallel QST registration is made with Revenu Québec using Form LM-1-V (Registration Application for GST/HST and QST), which allows a combined registration for both federal GST/HST and Quebec QST. The entity must also obtain a Quebec Establishment Number (NEQ) if it has a physical presence in Quebec; otherwise, a non-resident may register directly for QST where a supply is made in Quebec in the course of a business carried on in Quebec. All registrations require a Canadian mailing address or a designated agent in Canada for service of documents.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not provide a check-the-box classification regime. A limited partnership is a fiscally transparent person for income tax purposes; the partnership itself does not pay federal or Quebec income tax, but each partner, including a non-resident limited partner, is subject to Canadian tax on its share of partnership income attributable to a Canadian permanent establishment. For GST/HST and QST, a partnership is a separate ‘person’ and must register in its own name if its taxable supplies exceed the registration threshold; no formal pass-through election applies, but the partnership and its members may enter into joint and several liability arrangements for indirect taxes. There is no hybrid mismatch election mechanism available in Canada; hybrid mismatch rules apply compulsorily under Canadian domestic law and are not elective.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax (GST/HST) and Quebec Sales Tax (QST) — a dual federal-provincial value-added tax system
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 in taxable supplies (other than zero-rated supplies) worldwide within the preceding four consecutive calendar quarters or in a single calendar quarter in Canada; the same CAD 30,000 threshold applies separately for QST registration in Quebec. Once registered, a non-resident may claim input tax credits and input tax refunds for GST/QST paid on expenses attributable to its taxable supplies.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada has no real-time fiscal clearance or mandatory digital stamping system. The CRA requires that registrants retain electronic records in a readable and accessible format, and GST/HST invoices must contain specified particulars (supplier name, registration number, date, description, amount and tax charged). Quebec has progressively mandatory electronic invoicing for large enterprises and public-sector entities under Revenu Québec’s electronic invoicing initiative; however, this mandate is being phased and does not require an API-based transaction clearance or government pre-approval of invoices. A registered person may need to use a Revenu Québec-certified e-invoicing service provider when required.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to supplies of goods that are exported by the supplier, supplied to a non-resident recipient for use outside Canada, or supplied in the course of transporting goods to a destination outside Canada. For data center colocation services, the supply of server rack space, power, cooling, and related hosting services to a non-resident who uses the services partly or wholly outside Canada may be zero-rated only where the service is supplied to a non-resident and is not performed in whole or in part in Canada; colocation services actually rendered at the Quebec data center are generally subject to GST/HST and QST at the place of performance, and the exporter must obtain documentary evidence proving the service is performed outside Canada if zero-rating is claimed. For goods zero-rating, the supplier must retain evidence establishing that the goods were exported within a prescribed period and that the supplier did not make the goods available to the purchaser in Canada. Services that are ancillary to the supply of exported goods may also be zero-rated if the primary supply is zero-rated.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Canada Customs Invoice / Customs Export Declaration (Canada Border Services Agency – CSA approved form, eManifest or ACI export data)
Commercial invoice or service agreement indicating foreign destination and non-resident recipient
Bill of Lading (ocean, air, rail or truck waybill) showing final destination outside Canada
Proof of exportation issued by CBSA or a bonded carrier, including the customs export declaration number
CRA Form GST/HST Transfer or Foreign Recipient Certificate (if applicable, to support zero-rating of exported services or intangible property)
Bank transfer or wire record demonstrating payment by the non-resident recipient (not a mandatory condition for zero-rating, but used as supporting evidence)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The CRA and Revenu Québec may audit an exporter’s books for six years from the end of the reporting period. If zero-rated exports are claimed without proper supporting documentation, the tax authorities may reassess the supply as taxable, requiring GST/QST to be remitted on the full sale price with penalties and arrears interest, and may claw back any input tax credits claimed in connection with the supply. Willful participation in a false export claim can lead to penalties under the Excise Tax Act (e.g., subsection 285.1) of up to $25,000 plus fines up to $100,000, or a percentage of the tax evaded, and the Tax Court of Canada may impose a gross negligence penalty not exceeding 50% of the tax evaded. Criminal prosecution is available for fraudulent export schemes under section 380 of the Criminal Code, and the Quebec tax authority may impose separate penalties under the Tax Administration Act (CQLR c. A-6.002).

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) as the central bank and sole issuing authority for bank notes; prudential regulation and supervision of Schedule I chartered banks by the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI); anti-money-laundering and terrorist-financing supervision by the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC); cross-border currency and trade declaration reporting by the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA). Canada has no dedicated foreign-exchange-control agency because the Foreign Exchange Control Act was repealed in 1951 and the Canadian dollar is fully free-floating.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility of the Canadian dollar on both current-account and capital-account transactions. There are no non-resident conversion restrictions, no prior-authorization hurdles, and no blocked-funds mechanism for profit remittances, LP distribution remittances, loan repayments, or repatriation of contributed capital. The practical frictions for the Quebec LP are: (i) FINTRAC electronic-funds-transfer reporting for transfers at or above CAD 10,000; (ii) Canadian tax exposure of non-resident limited partners on Canadian-source business income allocations through the partnership (Part I of the Income Tax Act) and Part XIII withholding on treaty-relevant amounts such as interest, rents, and royalties, with rates normally reduced under the Canada-US treaty for US partners; (iii) the Investment Canada Act notification or review obligation where non-Canadian partners establish or acquire control of a Canadian data-center business; and (iv) settlement and pricing discipline, because the CAD/USD market is offshore and deep, and the LP should transact FX only with a regulated Canadian dealer or a CLS-participant bank to ensure compliant execution and settlement.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canadian law imposes no statutory repatriation timeline, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no surrender requirement for export proceeds to the central bank or any government authority. Export receipts in USD or other currencies may be held indefinitely in foreign-currency operating accounts at a Canadian Schedule I bank. For income-tax purposes, every settlement of foreign currency must be translated into CAD under section 39(1) of the Income Tax Act, and the LP should adopt and document a consistent translation policy (Bank of Canada noon rate or contractual spot rate) to support auditable FX gain or loss computation. Cross-border revenue from colocation rack-space licensing, bare-metal hosting, and managed services is generally zero-rated for GST/HST when supplied to a non-resident and not connected to real property situated in Quebec; to the extent a rack or cage arrangement is recharacterized as a right over Quebec real property, GST at 5% and QST at 9.975% may apply to that portion of the supply.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: National Bank of Canada (Banque Nationale du Canada)
National Bank of Canada (Banque Nationale du Canada)
Laurentian Bank of Canada (Banque Laurentienne du Canada)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: MEDIUM. Offshore digital EMIs (Wise, Airwallex, Currencycloud, and similar) are viable as supplementary collection and disbursement rails and for multicurrency treasury float, but they cannot replace a Schedule I operating account or the capital escrow account of the Quebec LP. Legal constraints: (i) an EMI providing payment services to Canadian residents is generally required to register as a money services business (MSB) with FINTRAC and to file suspicious-transaction and large-EFT reports; (ii) retail payment functions performed in Canada trigger Bank of Canada registration under the Retail Payment Activities Act (RPAA), which came into force in 2024, and most offshore EMIs access the Canadian market through agent arrangements with regulated processors; (iii) CAD-denominated settlement ultimately clears through Payments Canada (Lynx or ACSS) or through correspondent banks, and an unregulated EMI cannot obtain direct clearing membership; and (iv) the LP remains primarily responsible under PCMLTFA for the accuracy of beneficial-ownership and transaction information furnished to the EMI, and the EMI's foreign license (for example, FCA authorization in the United Kingdom) must be evidenced, monitored, and reverified periodically.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Hybrid onboarding with remote opening permitted under enhanced conditions. Under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act and the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Regulations, the bank must identify and verify the LP, the general partner, all authorized signatories, and every ultimate beneficial owner holding 25 percent or more of the partnership interests. Most Schedule I banks permit fully remote onboarding for a low-risk, standard-tier colocation LP using video identification, electronic signature, CRS and FATCA self-certification, and scanned corporate records, but the onboarding module typically requires: (i) a live video interview with the general partner's director or the LP's treasurer; (ii) the Quebec certificate of registration issued by the Registraire des entreprises du Quebec, the certified LP agreement, and a certified resolution of the general partner; and (iii) notarized, apostilled, or legalized identity documents for non-resident limited partners. Where a signatory is resident outside Canada, the bank may require a physical visit to its commercial banking centre in Montreal or Toronto or a verified appointment at the bank's correspondent office in the signatory's country of residence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial-ownership opacity: the LP is composed of a non-resident corporate general partner and a tiered chain of offshore limited partners without a transparent partnership register, triggering the bank's inability to verify ultimate beneficial ownership under PCMLTFA and a probable account-refusal decision.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Quebec certificate of registration and certified LP agreement; complete partner register showing each partner's legal name, address, jurisdiction, and percentage interest; annotated organizational chart flowing through every direct and indirect owner to the natural-person level; certified board resolutions of the general partner; beneficial-ownership self-certifications from every owner holding 25 percent or more; and source-of-capital evidence for initial escrow funding, comprising audited financial statements of the parent entity and a bank reference letter.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident signatory and partner nexus with FATF-identified or sanctions-flagged jurisdictions, which elevates onboarding to enhanced due diligence and triggers heightened reputational review.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified passports and a second government-issued photo identification document for every principal; proof of residential address dated within 90 days; a three-year relationship reference from a reputable bank where the principal already transacts; a notarized power of attorney appointing a Canadian resident authorized signatory with presence in Quebec; completed sanctions-prescreening and adverse-media records; and a written statement of the legitimate commercial purpose of the data-center colocation business.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Revenue-intake complexity: the LP expects payments from cryptocurrency miners, gambling-affiliated tenants, or shell sublessors, which the bank's enhanced due-diligence matrix flags as higher-risk commercial counterparties.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed colocation lease and rack-space agreements for each tenant; tenant KYC files comprising charter documents, government-issued licenses, and GST and QST registrations; evidence of physical assets such as owned or leased racks, environmental-control systems, utility invoices, and managed-service contracts; a six-month billing forecast demonstrating recurring moderate-value ACH payments and occasional SWIFT wires; and a compliance resolution of the general partner prohibiting enumerated prohibited-industry customers.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital-injection velocity: large, lumpy USD or CAD deposits into the capital escrow account that are inconsistent with the stated capital-call schedule and may trigger a suspicious-transaction report.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Capital-call notices with payment due dates; the LP's private offering or formation documents; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds reports for each contributing partner; bank statements of the remitting account showing corresponding debits; a flow-of-funds schedule for the data-center build-out; and a solicitor's opinion confirming the escrow, pass-through, and business-purpose characterization under Quebec and Canadian law.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound partner capital injections should be executed by SWIFT MT103 customer credit transfers in the partner's home currency or by Payments Canada ACSS or Lynx domestic EFT where the remitter holds a Canadian account. Each transfer must state a clear purpose-of-payment description in SWIFT field 70 or the bank's EFT reference field, such as CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION - CA_LP or CAPITAL CALL - DATA CENTER, and the receiving bank will map the transaction to the applicable Bank of Canada balance-of-payments classification code for an inward direct investment. The receiving bank files a FINTRAC large electronic-funds-transfer report for inflows at or above CAD 10,000, so the LP must concurrently provide the capital-call notice, the partner-register excerpt, and the remitter's bank statement to evidence source of funds. Where a non-Canadian partner makes an inward direct investment through the LP, the Investment Canada Act requires a notification within 30 days after the establishment of a new Canadian business or the filing of a notification or review application before implementation where an existing Canadian business is acquired, and the escrow release schedule should be conditioned on compliance with that filing. For USD contributions, the remitter should execute through the bank's US-dollar clearing tier or a CLS-participant counterparty to obtain effective same-day value and to avoid a two-day correspondent float.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade and operating disbursements should be cleared as follows: (i) SWIFT MT103 customer transfers for cross-border vendor payments, including hardware importation, sublessors, and international carriers, for amounts at or above CAD 10,000, with invoice and lease-reference details attached; (ii) Lynx, the high-value real-time gross-settlement system operated by Payments Canada, for domestic CAD payments above CAD 25,000 or same-day-critical obligations, including GST and QST remittances to the Canada Revenue Agency and Revenu Quebec; (iii) ACSS automated-clearing settlement for recurring monthly ACH debits and credits covering colocation tenant billings and payroll; (iv) commercial letters of credit governed by UCP 600, issued by the Schedule I bank through SWIFT MT700 with MT707 amendments, for confirmed equipment purchases into the data-center facility, including standby letters of credit for utility capacity and interconnection commitments; and (v) the bank's US-dollar correspondent network for USD wire transfers. Each outbound MT103 must carry a complete purpose-of-payment narrative, must be matched to the underlying commercial invoice, and must be retained in the LP's AML file for FINTRAC transaction-reporting and audit purposes.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forwards (USD/CAD, EUR/CAD) under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement or the bank's master forward-currency contract, with tenors up to 24 months.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) restricted solely to receivables denominated in emerging-market currencies that are not freely deliverable, such as CNY, INR, and BRL; CAD-based NDFs are not market standard given the full convertibility of the Canadian dollar.
Cross-currency swaps (USD/CAD) used to match long-dated colocation lease income streams with debt-service and capital-expenditure obligations.
Vanilla FX options (USD/CAD calls and puts) for asymmetric hedging of tenant-rent volatility and capex budget certainty.
FX swaps comprising simultaneous spot and forward legs for short-dated treasury liquidity management and for minimizing settlement risk on cross-border capital calls.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quebec Annual Enterprise Declaration (Déclaration annuelle under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (Gouvernement du Québec)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by the anniversary date of the enterprise's original registration; any change in partner, general partner, registered address or activity must be reported within 60 days of the event.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing exposes the partnership to administrative penalties of approximately CAD 200–2,000; persistent non-filing can lead to administrative dissolution or strike-off of the registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Calendar-year partnerships: on or before March 31 of the year following the fiscal period-end; non-calendar-year fiscal periods: within six months after fiscal year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Income Tax Act s.162(7) penalty of CAD 25 per partner per day (minimum CAD 100; maximum CAD 2,500), plus potential gross-negligence penalties under s.163(2).

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Partner Register Audit and Confirmation (internal statutory books maintenance)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General partner; books available for inspection by the Registraire des entreprises du Québec and Revenu Québec
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Simultaneously with the annual declaration; updated within 15 days of any transfer or change in limited-partner interests.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance exposes the general partner to civil claims from limited partners; knowingly false registry information may trigger monetary penalties of up to CAD 10,000 and administrative strike-off proceedings.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory audit is required solely by the Civil Code of Québec for a private limited partnership; a certified audit becomes compulsory only if a partner is a reporting issuer, a lender or partnership agreement requires audited financial statements, or the partnership becomes subject to a prescribed regulated-sector audit obligation.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS for public-reporting or parent-reporting LPs; otherwise Canadian ASPE is an acceptable private-enterprise GAAP basis; the partnership must maintain accrual-based books and records reconciling to the T5013 allocations.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Quebec does not require a standalone UBO registry return for a limited partnership; each annual declaration must confirm the general partner and registered address, and the partnership's internal register must record every limited partner, capital contribution and transfer. The T5013 then discloses Canadian-resident allocations and principal partner ownership to CRA for each taxation year.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (limited and general partners, including capital contributions and distributions)
Register of Directors (applicable when the general partner is a corporation)
Minute Book (general-partner resolutions and annual confirmation records)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 150–450 per year for a registered office address in Quebec plus provincial registered-agent representation
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 7,000–22,000 for a Tier-3/4 colocation LP if a lender or partner agreement triggers a certified independent audit

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 26.5% combined general corporate rate (15% federal Part I + 11.5% Quebec provincial; the LP itself is fiscally transparent and this rate applies to corporate general partners on their allocable share)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Quebec 'Tax Holiday for Large Investment Projects' (10-year provincial income tax exemption for eligible investments of CAD 100M+ in designated sectors, including data centres); federal Accelerated Investment Incentive and immediate expensing for eligible depreciable property (CCA Classes 1, 43.2, 46); Quebec E-Business Place credit (legacy) not generally available to colocation operators; partnership income is taxed at partner level with integration.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Federal: T5013 Partnership Information Return (with Schedule 50 partner allocation) filed via CRA EFILE/NETFILE (XML); Quebec: CO-17 Declaration of a Partnership filed via Revenu Quebec's EDT (Electronic Declaration Transmission).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (fiscal period; mandatory for every LP carrying on business in Canada or with Canadian-source income)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Federal T5013: within 5 months after the partnership's fiscal period end (e.g., 2024-12-31 fiscal end -> 2025-05-31); Quebec CO-17: within 6 months after the fiscal period end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Partnership legal name and BN (Business Number); Quebec NEQ (Numero d'entreprise du Quebec).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners must ensure the LP is registered for the federal BN and Quebec NEQ; the LP must appoint a Canadian resident agent for service if it has no Canadian office.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross business income from colocation rack-space leasing and bare-metal hosting services.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Classify recurring rack-space fees as business/rental income; distinguish 'true leases' of real property from service-based hosting; a non-resident partner's share is taxable as Canadian-source business income and is reported on the partner's Part I return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Rental revenue derived from passive leasing of floor space/cages/power capacity.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the arrangement is characterized as a lease of real property, non-resident partners may be exposed to Part XIII withholding on 'rent' under ITA 212(1)(d) unless treaty relief applies; service-heavy colocation agreements should be documented to avoid recharacterization.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Each limited partner's name, address, tax ID (SIN/BN/foreign tax ID), and allocated share of income/loss, capital contributed, and draws.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Furnish foreign tax identification numbers and residence addresses; attach the Quebec allocation schedule if the LP has multi-province nexus; failure to identify non-resident partners triggers reporting under T5013 and possible Part XIII assessment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: T5013 Box 815 / CO-17 Resultat de l'exercice
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Current-year partnership net income (loss) allocated to all partners.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The allocated income retains its character in the hands of each non-resident partner; a non-resident partner carrying on business in Canada through the LP must file an NR6 (if electing to file under ITA 216? Actually NR6 is for rental) — I'll simplify: must file a Canadian Part I return (T1 or T2) by the filing deadline to report the allocated income; quarterly tax instalments may apply.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Federal: late T5013 is penalized under ITA 162(7) at CAD 25/day (minimum CAD 100, maximum CAD 2,500 per partner affected); 'large partnerships' (gross revenue over CAD 20M) face CAD 250/day up to CAD 25,000. Quebec: Revenu Quebec imposes CDN 25/day (minimum CDN 100, maximum CDN 2,500) for late CO-17, plus interest; partners' deductions (e.g., home office, registrations) may be disallowed until the return is filed. Willful non-filing is prosecuted under ITA 238/239 with fines up to 200% of tax evaded and imprisonment up to 5 years.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% statutory Part XIII rate (ITA 212(2)) on Canadian-source dividends; for the LP, distribution of profits to a non-resident limited partner is NOT a dividend subject to Part XIII — it is a flow-through allocation of Canadian business income reportable on the partner's Part I return. Where a corporate partner later declares a dividend from Canadian earnings, the 25% (or treaty-reduced) rate applies.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To apply a tax treaty (e.g., Canada-US): (1) obtain a Certificate of Residence (TRC) from the foreign tax authority for the beneficial owner; (2) complete Form NR301 (Application for a Reduction in the Amount of Non-Resident Tax Withheld) or the simplified NR301-S; (3) deliver the TRC and NR301 to the Canadian payer (or partnership) before remittance so the payer withholds at the treaty rate; (4) maintain supporting ownership/commercial-substance evidence; (5) if tax was over-withheld, file Form NR7-R within two years to claim a refund from the CRA. Quebec respects federal treaty applications; no separate Quebec TRC is required for Part XIII, but Quebec income tax treaty application follows the same federal DTA network.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory Part XIII: interest 25% (ITA 212(1)(b)) and royalty 25% (ITA 212(1)(d)); Canada-US treaty: interest 0% (arm's length; exempt under Article XI after the Fifth Protocol); royalty 0% for copyright and certain cultural rights, 10% for industrial patents/know-how (Article XII); other Canadian DTAs (e.g., UK, France) generally cap dividends at 5%/15%, interest at 10-15%, royalties at 10%.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: T106 (Information Return of Non-Arm's Length Transactions with Non-Residents) must be filed when the aggregate value of transactions with a non-resident related party exceeds CAD 50,000 in a reporting period. CRA contemporaneous TP documentation (master/local file-style) is administratively required for 'large' taxpayers (gross revenue over CAD 50M and non-arm's-length cross-border transactions over CAD 5M); all taxpayers must maintain reasonable records under ITA 247(4).
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada has no Economic Substance Regulations in the BVI/offshore sense. Substance is nevertheless central: (i) GAAR (ITA 245) and Quebec's anti-avoidance provisions can recharacterize a Quebec LP that lacks commercial substance; (ii) treaty relief requires the non-resident partner to be the beneficial owner with a real Canadian PE (attribution of profits under OECD Article 7); (iii) a 'shell' LP with no premises, employees, or business activity in Quebec is exposed to reassessment of income, denial of treaty benefits, and penalties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion (Income Tax Act s. 239 / Quebec Tax Administration Act)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Wilfully evading or attempting to evade federal or Quebec income tax, including omitting allocable income, fabricating colocation operating expenses, or making false statements in T5013/CO-17.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal prosecution: fine of 50%-200% of the tax evaded and imprisonment up to 5 years (ITA 239(1)); Quebec: minimum fine of 50% and up to 200% plus imprisonment; CRA 'Diligence' program referrals to the Public Prosecution Service can freeze assets and require an audit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and senior officers are jointly and severally liable under ITA 227.1 for unremitted withholdings (payroll, Part XIII); where fraud is proven, the corporate veil is pierced, exposing personal assets; travel is restricted (CRA can obtain a court order and the Canada Border Services Agency detains at the border for outstanding warrants; serious evasion draws criminal travel bans and extradition risk).

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Unfiled Partnership / Information Returns & Repeat Non-Compliance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Repeatedly failing to file the T5013/CO-17, T106 transfer-pricing information return, or NR4/NR6 slips despite CRA/Revenu Quebec demand letters.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Escalating civil penalties: ITA 162(7) CAD 25-250/day per partner; ITA 247(3) transfer-pricing penalty of 10% of the net adjustment where the adjustment exceeds the greater of CAD 5M or 10% of gross revenue; Quebec civil penalties under s. 56 of the Tax Administration Act; interest accrues on all balances.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of a corporate general partner can be held liable for the LP's unremitted withholdings and penalties; a 'failure to file' can result in Revenu Quebec issuing a certificate of prosecution, leading to a travel ban against the responsible partner and seizure of personal holdings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / GAAR Recharacterization (ITA 245; Quebec General Anti-Avoidance Rule)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Establishing a Quebec LP solely to access the large-investment tax holiday or treaty benefits with no real data-centre operations, no employees, no risk, and no commercial substance; circular financing with related foreign entities to manufacture losses.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The CRA/Revenu Quebec disregards the partnership, reassesses on a 'look-through' basis, denies the tax holiday and treaty reductions, imposes gross-negligence penalties of 50% of the understated tax (ITA 163(2)), and charges interest from the original filing date.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Promoters and directors may be named as 'planners' under GAAR with third-party liability; courts have lifted the veil to impose restitution on shareholders who stripped the LP's assets; serious cases carry criminal fraud charges under the Criminal Code (s. 380) with imprisonment up to 14 years and travel bans.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting monthly ACH/SWIFT colocation payments from anonymous shell clients, failing to complete a risk assessment, not registering as a 'money services business' where the LP processes third-party payments, or failing to report suspicious transactions (STR) and large cash/virtual-currency transactions (LCTR) — data-centre colocation is low-risk but payment intermediaries trigger obligations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: FINTRAC administrative monetary penalties up to CAD 500,000 for entities and CAD 100,000 for individuals per violation; CRA can freeze accounts linked to unreported virtual-currency proceeds; criminal proceedings for knowingly dealing with proceeds of crime under Criminal Code s. 462.31.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers are personally liable for AML failures (PCMLTFA s. 74.1); violations can result in Canadian travel bans for foreign directors, denial of visa applications, and extradition for predicate offences; the corporate veil is pierced where the LP is a facade for money laundering.
